answer: A port pays agents to certify ferrous cargo for a voyage through an inlet. Each certification locks a separate bond B; a ledger prevents collateral reuse and caps payment at G. After submission, an independent inspector audits it with probability p before bond release. False reports lose B; set pB>G. Thus extra identities cannot reuse one bond, and each fraudulent claim has negative expected profit. This assumes unpredictable sampling, trustworthy cargo measurements and enforceable slashing; a wealthy attacker may still pay to disrupt.
